Present
 Sri. Keshava.K., B.A., Ll.B.,

Chief Judicial Magistrate,
 Bengaluru.

Dated this 06th day of November, 2024
 C.C.No.9263 of 2020
Complainant : State by the Police Sub Inspector ,
 Basavanagudi Women police station,
 Bengaluru.

[By Assistant Public Prosecutor]
 - Vs -
Accused Vijay Kumar Shetty,
 Aged about 45 years,
 R/at.Narsi Nivas, close to
 Chitrapu school, Mulki,
 Mangalore.

[By Sri.Shakeel Ahmed .. Advocate]
 Judgment

The charge sheet has been filed in this case by the Police Sub Inspector of Basavanagudi Women police station against the accused for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 506 of IPC.

. In briefly the case of the prosecution is as follows:-
It is the case of the prosecution that, the accused married C.W.1 Smt.Kirthy Shetty on 14.05.2006 at Buntara Bhavan, Mulki, Mangalore thereafter the C.W.1 was residing with the accused in her matrimonial house at R.T.Nagar, where the accused with an Smt. Kirthy Shetty vs Vijay on 6 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163588430/
1 intention to commit an offence, being addicted to consuming alcohol, smoking,
consuming zarda day in and day out harassed C.W.1 physically and mentally and failed to look after C.W.1 and their son, further the accused was in the habit of taking money from C.W.1 and not returning it back to her and the accused used to steal money from the house for consuming alcohol, though the accused went to Saudi Arabia for work, he demanded C.W.1 to give him Rs.60,000/- and physically and mentally harassed C.W.1 by abusing her in filthy language and assaulted to her.

Further the accused threatened C.W.1 to do away with her life if she did not give him money as demanded and therefore the C.W.1 lodged the complaint against accused before the Basavanagudi Women Police seeking necessary action against him in accordance with law.
3. On the basis of the said complaint given by C.W.1, the complainant police have registered the case under Crime No.01/2020 and sent FIR to this Court and to their concerned higher authorities.

Thereafter, the complainant police have visited the spot and conducted the spot mahazar in the presence of the panch witnesses, herein after recorded the statements of witnesses who availed in the station subsequently who availed where the said mahazars have been drawn, after completion of the investigation the IO has arived at a conclusion that there are sufficient materials as to prosecute the accused , for which charge sheet has been filed for the above said offences.

4. After filing of the charge sheet, this Court registered the case is as numbered above, before that the accused person was enlarged on bail in Crl.Petition No.2928/2020, subsequently in persuance of summons the C.C.9263/2020 accused appeared before this Court and was enlarged on bail,
meanwhile copies of the charge sheet and other prosecution papers were duly supplied as required under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing both sides, this court found that there were sufficient reasons so as to frame charge against the accused, therefore charge was framed and read over and explained to the accused in the language known to him, after understanding the same he denied the same and claimed to be tried, accordingly, proceeded with trial.
5. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined one witness who is said to be victim as P.W.1 and got marked two documents at Ex.P-1 and 2.

As there are no any incriminating materials forth coming against the accused, as to which summoning of remaining witnesses would no purpose to serve and therefore CW-2 to 6 ordered to be given up by rejecting the submission made by the learned PP.
Consequently, recording of statement of accused as required under section 313 of Cr.P.C also dispensed with.
6. Heard both side arguments, in compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C., bail bond were obtained from the accused.

7. In view of above said facts and circumstances the following points that would arise for my consideration are as follows:-
POINTS FOR CONSIDERATION Smt. Kirthy Shetty vs Vijay on 6 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163588430/
2 1.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused married C.W.1 Smt.Kirthy Shetty on 14.05.2006 at Buntara Bhavan, Mulki,
Mangalore and after marriage while C.W.1 was residing with the accused at the matrimonial house at R.T.Nagar, the accused with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of the intention, being addicted to bad vices such as smoking,
consuming alcohol and zarda day in and day out harassed C.W.1 physically and mentally and failed to look after C.W.1 and their son, further C.C.9263/2020 the accused was in the habit of taking money from C.W.1 and not returning it back to her and the accused used to steal money from the house for consumig alcohol, though the accused went to Saudi Arabia for work, he demanded C.W.1 to give you Rs.60,000/-
and physically and mentally harassed C.W.1 thereby the accused have committed an offence punishable under section 498A of IPC?
2.

Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that while C.W.1 was residing at the matrimonial home with the accused at R.T.Nagar the accused abused C.W.1 in filthy languag knowingly that it would give provocation to C.W.1to breach public peace and thereby the accused committed the offence of "intentional insult" punishable U/s 504 of IPC?

3. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that while C.W.1 was residing at the matrimonial home with the accused at R.T.Nagar the accused criminally intimidated to do away with the life of C.W1 if she did not give him money as demanded and thereby the accused has committed an offence of "criminal intimidation" punishable U/s 506 of IPC?
4. What Order?
8. My answers to the above points are as under:
Point Nos.1 to 3 : In the 'Negative' Point No.4 : As per the final order, for the following:-
REASONS 9. Point No.1 to 3: These points are taken up together for common discussion in order to avoid the repetation of facts.
10.
In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined the complainant/C.W.1 as P.W.1 and got marked two documents on her behalf as Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2.

The C.W.1 being complainant as well as C.C.9263/2020 victim in this case is examined as P.W.1 and Ex.P.1 and 2 documents got marked on her behalf, as far as appreciation of oral and documentary evidence is concerned P.W.1 is the complainant by name Kirthy Shetty deposed that the accused is her husband and her marriage was solemnized with the accused on 14.05.2006 at Buntara Bhavana Mulki, Mangalore.

Further she deposed that after her marriage with the accused she was residing at the matrimonial house with the Smt. Kirthy Shetty vs Vijay on 6 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163588430/
3 accused at R.T.nagar and out of wedlock they have a son and they are living together in cordial terms and the accused did not extend any physical and mental harassment towards her.

sentences.text: She further deposed that she deposed that she has not lodged complaint against the accused persons.

She deposed that when she had been to Basavanagudi Women PS in the year 2020 police took her signatures on two documents and she does not know the contents of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 and police did not draw any mahazar before her presence as per Ex.P.2.

She identified her signature on Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 but she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P-1 and 2 as to which when learned Assistant Public Prosecutor treated this witness as hostile and with the permission of the court,
cross-examined her even in that process also learned A.P.P. failed to elicit anything from her mouth.

She further deposed that her marriage with the accused ended in divorce on 14.08.2024.
11.

As the first informant/complainant P.W.1 being the material witness in this case has not supported the case of the prosecution and as she turned hostile by giving a complete go-bye statement, due to which other prosecution witness were given up, as it would serve no purpose to summon the other witnesses, during the course of prosecution evidence two documents got marked as Ex.P1 and P.2.
So far as Ex.P1 is the complaint and Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar, but the prosecution witness did not support the contents which are mentioned C.C.9263/2020 in the same

,
therefore whatever the suspicious circumstances pleaded while framing of charge remained as same.

On considering these facts herein no incriminating materials forthcoming against the accused persons and the prosecution has not established the ingredients of the alleged offences against the accused however herein no positive evidence to prove the guilt of the accused , for which this Court is of the considered opinion that prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.

Hence, benefit of doubt goes to the accused , for which I answer point Nos.1 to 3 in the 'Negative'.
12. Point No.4:

In view of my findings on point Nos.1 to 3 and reasons assigned therein, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Acting under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused is not found guilty and he is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Secs.498A, 504, 506 of IPC.
The bail bond executed by the accused stands cancelled.

In compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C. the bail bond executed by the accused is ordered to be continued in force for six months or till issuance of notice in respect of any appeal [if preferred] against the present Judgment before the Appellate Court.
(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcript revised, corrected and signed & then pronounced in the Open court on this the 06 th day of November, 2024.)
(KESHAVA.K) XXXII Addl.Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru.
